literal: Intense hunger and unceasing disease and destructive enmity not entering, that which functions is a country.
translation: A true country is that which functions without ever being afflicted by intense hunger, unceasing disease, and destructive enmity.
modern: மிக்க பசியும், நீங்காத நோயும், அழிவு செய்யும் பகையும் வந்து சேராமல் நடைபெறுவதே நாடாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the essential qualities of a prosperous and peaceful nation. A true country must be free from three major scourges: extreme hunger (famine), persistent epidemics or diseases, and destructive external or internal enemies. The word 'உறுபசி' refers to intense, widespread hunger, while 'ஓவாப் பிணி' denotes diseases that never seem to leave the population. 'செறுபகை' represents hostile forces that seek to destroy. Only when a land is naturally free from these three afflictions can it function successfully as a true nation.
